sample_data.method: bundled JSON file (household_PUB-01.json), loaded automatically by run_demo.py
sample_data.reset_instructions: The fixture file is never mutated by run_demo.py; simply re-run run_demo.py to regenerate all outputs from a clean state.

problem_solving_method: Modelled the meter as a strict day-by-day ledger: each day's units are charged in full at the slab the calendar month's cumulative total reaches after that day, plus 5% VAT on the energy amount; a recharge adds money and, only if it is the first recharge seen in that calendar month, also deducts the 42 BDT demand charge and 40 BDT meter rent. The run-out and recharge-to-target calculators reuse this same slab/reset logic projected forward. The habit comparison runs identical daily consumption under both recharge policies and verifies energy plus VAT always match, so any cost difference can only come from how many months triggered a first-recharge fixed charge.

R1.evidence: household_PUB-01.json - 181 days (2026-01-01 to 2026-06-30), 18 recharges, includes a light month (January), a heavy summer month (May), and a large last-week recharge (June 25 and 29)

R2.evidence: tariff_engine.rebuild_ledger() -> PUB-01_balance_ledger.csv and PUB-01_balance_chart.png (balance line with every recharge marked and labelled)

R3.evidence: tariff_engine.project_runout_date() and tariff_engine.recharge_needed() -> PUB-01_full_results.json (run-out date and full energy/higher-slab/fixed/VAT breakdown)

R4.evidence: tariff_engine.simulate_habit() run for both 'low_balance' and 'monthly' habits over the three comparison months -> PUB-01_full_results.json, cross-checked against all 25 published sample households to confirm every cost difference is an exact multiple of 82.00 BDT

major_design_decisions: Charge each day's units in full at the single slab the month's cumulative total reaches after that day, rather than splitting a day's units across two slabs, for a deterministic and auditable ledger.

Apply the 42 BDT demand charge and 40 BDT meter rent strictly on the first recharge event of each calendar month, not on a fixed calendar date, as required by the problem statement and needed for a meaningful habit comparison.
Break the recharge-to-target amount into a flat baseline energy cost (lowest slab rate) plus a separate higher-slab surcharge, so the family can see how much of the bill is caused by heavy usage.
known_limitations: No live web frontend yet - current submission demonstrates all four requirements via a Python script (run_demo.py) against the bundled household fixture.
Only one household (PUB-01) is bundled and demonstrated end-to-end, though the engine has been validated against all 25 published sample households for the habit-comparison invariant.
No deployment or persistence layer yet.

ai_tools_used.used_for: Designing and implementing the tariff/billing engine, the day-by-day ledger rebuild, the run-out-date and recharge-breakdown calculators, the habit-comparison simulator, the balance chart, and the repository documentation.
ai_tools_used.how_output_was_verified: Hand-checked individual ledger rows against the stated tariff (e.g. confirming the 82 BDT fixed charge lands only on the first recharge of a month), and ran the habit comparison across all 25 published sample households to confirm every cost difference is an exact multiple of 82.00 BDT, matching the clarification that recharge timing cannot create a fabricated slab saving.

declaration: The information above is complete and truthful to the best of the team's knowledge.
